comparisons.peer_summary: The company may not be able to fully realize expected benefits or synergies from acquisitions or other business initiatives in the expected time frames, or at all.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS explicitly disclose the risk that strategic initiatives, particularly acquisitions, may fail to deliver expected value or synergies within the anticipated timeframe. MS states it may be unable to fully capture expected value from acquisitions and joint ventures, noting that certain acquisitions may subject the business to new risks. GS mirrors this by stating it may not be able to fully realize expected benefits or synergies from acquisitions or other business initiatives in the expected time frames, or at all. Both disclosures highlight the uncertainty surrounding the realization of transactional value.

sentences.text: We may be unable to fully capture the expected value from acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures, partnerships, minority stakes or strategic alliances, and certain acquisitions may subject our business to new or increased risk.
• We may not be able to fully realize the expected benefits or synergies from acquisitions or other business initiatives in the time frames we expect, or at all.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks of New Business Initiatives and Acquisitions
comparisons.peer_summary: The company engages in new business initiatives, including selective acquisitions, which expose it to enhanced risks such as regulatory scrutiny, reputational harm, credit and operational risks, and legal uncertainties. Success depends on the ability to integrate acquired businesses, realize synergies, and manage complex transitions; failures have resulted in unanticipated costs, losses, and write-downs, as seen in the 2024 dispositions of GreenSky and the GM credit card program, and may adversely affect results of operations.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS link the inability to capture value from acquisitions to the exposure to new or enhanced risks, including operational and reputational harms. MS notes that certain acquisitions may subject its business to 'new or increased risk' alongside the failure to capture value. GS expands on this by listing specific enhanced risks associated with new business initiatives and acquisitions, such as regulatory scrutiny, reputational concerns, and operational risks, stating that failure to execute these initiatives could lead to unanticipated costs, losses, and negative reputational effects.

sentences.text: We may be unable to fully capture the expected value from acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures, partnerships, minority stakes or strategic alliances, and certain acquisitions may subject our business to new or increased risk.

New business initiatives expose us to new and enhanced risks, including risks associated with dealing with governmental entities, reputational concerns arising from dealing with different types of clients, business partners, counterparties and investors, greater regulatory scrutiny of these activities, increased credit-related, market, sovereign and operational risks, risks arising from accidents or acts of terrorism, and reputational concerns with the manner in which certain assets are being operated or held or in which we interact with these clients, business partners, counterparties and investors.
If and to the extent we are unable to successfully execute those initiatives, we may incur unanticipated costs and losses, and face other adverse consequences, such as negative reputational effects.

comparisons.peer_summary: Management's ability to address strategic priorities affects the company's capacity to develop resources, control expenses, and return capital. Failure to devise effective plans, meet client expectations, allocate capital appropriately, assess principal investments, conduct due diligence on acquisitions, address ESG concerns, react to market changes, or enhance resources could adversely affect these objectives.
comparisons.comparison: MS and JPM both identify the execution of strategic priorities and the due diligence/integration of acquisitions as key factors in capturing value. MS warns of the inability to capture expected value from acquisitions, divestitures, and joint ventures. JPM similarly highlights that management's effectiveness in conducting appropriate due diligence on prospective business acquisitions and effectively integrating newly-acquired businesses is critical to addressing strategic priorities. Both firms frame acquisition success as dependent on management's strategic execution capabilities.
